A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can improve accuracy by using well-trained classifiers selection unit, which learns to select the best classifiers from a large pool, instead of all classifiers, to make the decision for a given test instance.

, by using a well trained selection unit (referees or gating) we can get as good accuracy as using all base classifiers (to get their decision) but using much less number of base classifiers and also improve accuracy, and this is especially true in cases where none of the base classifier has high accuracy.
the gating system is more suitable when we have a large pool of classifiers to choose from, whereas referees would be more appropriate for a small pool.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by using a selection mechanism, we can achieve better accuracy with fewer number of base classifiers.

, by using a small number of base classifiers, we get a good improvement in accuracy and also the system becomes more robust to noise in the training set and to the addition of irrelevant features to the data set.
, by learning the selection units (i.e., referees or gating), we are able to improve accuracy of the base classifiers, and also reduce the number of base classifier used in the system.
